rules.action: Radial access is the standard approach for all PCI. Reduces bleeding, vascular complications, and mortality compared with femoral.
EBU or XB-type guide for left coronary system. Select curve to match aortic root size — EBU 3.5 or XB 3.5 for most adults.
Judkins Right first choice for RCA. Amplatz Left if additional backup force is needed.
Judkins Right first; escalate to Amplatz only if support insufficient. Deep-seating or GEC preferred over aggressive guide engagement.
rules.caution: Amplatz carries higher ostial trauma risk in tortuous/angulated RCA.

rules.action: Consider guide extension catheter (GEC) rather than escalating guide stiffness to improve device deliverability through tortuous or angulated segments.
Large-lumen guide (≥7Fr) required for LM PCI; 8Fr preferred for complex bifurcation techniques. EBU or XB for left coronary engagement. Confirm non-dampened waveform before wiring.
Confirm cardiac surgical backup availability. Non-emergent LM PCI should be performed by experienced, adequately equipped teams (≥20 LM PCI/year per operator).
Prioritise coaxial alignment over backup force. JR4/Hockey Stick for right-sided grafts; AL1/left coronary bypass for left-sided. GEC useful when ostial engagement is inadequate.
Strongly prefer PCI of the native coronary over the graft if technically feasible.
Radial access advised for calcified lesion PCI to reduce bleeding risk, particularly when atherectomy or IVL is planned.

Plan dual-access strategy: radial for PCI + femoral for large-bore MCS device. If femoral needed, use ultrasound and fluoroscopy guidance routinely. Minimise contrast; treat culprit only if multivessel disease.
rules.caution: Do not delay culprit treatment to place MCS if the patient is actively deteriorating — proceed in parallel.

rules.action: Size arterial access for potential MCS insertion: IABP 7–8Fr; Impella CP 14Fr; Impella 5.5 21Fr (axillary); VA-ECMO 15–21Fr arterial. Assess peripheral vascular disease before committing to large-bore access.
